title: Zero-dependency core
question: Should Doubt keep its core free of runtime dependencies?
verdict: Keep the validator, renderer, installer, and Action on Node built-ins until a measured use case justifies a dependency.

nodes.label: Explicit scope
nodes.text: The contributor contract defines Doubt as a zero-dependency Node CLI and portable Agent Skill.

nodes.label: Current contract coverage
nodes.text: The deterministic evidence-contract suite passes all twelve committed adversarial cases.

nodes.label: Maintenance pressure
nodes.text: The renderer owns its full HTML, CSS, graph drawing, filtering, and source-panel behavior in one source file.

nodes.label: Qualification
nodes.text: Passing structural mutations does not prove source truth or extraction fidelity.

nodes.label: Missing evidence
nodes.text: No measured user workflow yet shows that a dependency would remove enough complexity to justify its supply-chain and install cost.

edges.note: The current portability promise is explicit and already implemented.
The built-in implementation already enforces the narrow structural contract.
Avoiding dependencies transfers interface and rendering maintenance into the repository.
The green suite has a deliberately narrow interpretation.
A concrete workflow benchmark should decide when the constraint stops paying for itself.

sources.title: Doubt contributor guide
sources.excerpt: Doubt is a zero-dependency Node.js CLI plus a portable Agent Skill. Keep the core local-first, provider-independent, and fail-closed on source traceability.

sources.title: Evidence-contract benchmark
sources.excerpt: 20/20 cases passed (100%). This benchmark measures structural traceability and safe rendering. It does not measure whether a source is true or whether an AI extracted it faithfully.
